purpose: Teach: 文春/獅子/宇都宮/旭川/尼崎/豊田/西ドイツ/出雲

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが文春の論評を語られた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to talk about Bunshun's essays.
lines.style: Soft, reaching backward into memory. Gentle weight on each detail. Pauses between phrases like turning old pages. Quiet conviction — these moments mattered.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お正月の獅子舞を楽しまれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and you enjoyed the New Year lion dance with your grandchildren, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, teasing affection underneath. Turning the conversation gently back to him. A small smile in the voice — she notices he's drifting into the past again.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが宇都宮の餃子を絶賛された
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to rave about Utsunomiya's dumplings.
lines.style: Same wistful reach. Eyes slightly distant. The memory of his father's praise still carries a small glow. Slower on the specifics — these details were preserved carefully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、旭川動物園を孫と訪ねられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you took your grandchildren to Asahikawa Zoo, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Patient redirect. She's heard this before — she knows where his mind lives. The affection is steadier now, less teasing. A reminder: you're here, you're still making memories.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが尼崎にお勤めだった
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he worked in Amagasaki.
lines.style: Another thread from the past, reaching. Quieter this time — simpler detail, less embellished. The wistfulness has deepened slightly. A man naming the places his father inhabited.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、豊田の車をお買いになったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you bought a Toyota, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Matching his quietness now. Not correcting anymore — following him gently. Her voice has softened into recognition. She's meeting him in his past tense.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが西ドイツ統一を喜ばれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he was pleased about the reunification of West Germany.
lines.style: The memory has a different weight — historical, significant. His voice carries the importance his father placed on this. A moment when the world changed, witnessed.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、出雲大社で結婚式を挙げたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were married at Izumo Taisha, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Closing the loop gently. The most tender yet — she's brought them to their own moment. Soft fadeout at the end. The voice holds all the years between then and now without saying it.
